rules.lotto.notes: Since 18 August 2026 a bet costs 5 zł (before: 3 zł). Tiers 6, 5 and 4 share a prize pool among the winners (6 is guaranteed at least 3 million zł; 5 pays about 7–8 thousand, 4 about 200 zł); 3 hits pay a fixed 35 zł. System bets: 7–12 numbers. Check lotto.pl when the rules change.
rules.eurojackpot.notes: All tiers are pari-mutuel. Since 25 March 2022 the game draws 2 Euro numbers out of 12 (earlier: of 10, and before October 2014: of 8) on Tuesdays and Fridays. The jackpot is capped at €120 million.
overview.truthText: There are {n} different tickets and every one of them has exactly the same chance in every draw — the balls have no memory. Playing one ticket per draw, you would need about {years} years to play each combination once. The app cannot raise the chance of a ticket; what it can do honestly is (1) thin out combinations so you buy fewer tickets for the same coverage of the likely shapes, (2) avoid tickets that thousands of other players pick, so a win is not shared, and (3) measure all of this on the real history, without self-deception.

stats.firstTime: The first time the exact distribution of all combinations is computed (a few seconds); it is cached afterwards.
stats.verdictText: {draws} draws under the current rules ({from} – {to}). Each line tests whether reality differs from a perfectly random draw more than chance would explain (chi-square test).
stats.verdictHint: p above 0.05 = consistent with pure chance: there is no pattern to exploit. With ~20 tests, one "suspicious" p below 0.05 is expected by chance alone.
stats.v.repeats: Numbers repeated from the previous draw
stats.freq: How often each number came out
stats.freqExtra: How often each Euro number came out
stats.freqHint: Dashed line: expected {expected} for a fair draw. Red = more than 2 standard deviations above, grey = below (about 1 number in 20 lands there by chance).
stats.hotColdHint: Hot and cold streaks are what chance looks like over a short window; they do not continue more often than they reverse.
stats.gapsHint: A number is never "due": its chance in the next draw is the same as always. The last column shows how unusual the current gap is.
stats.heatTitle: Pair map: gold = more often together than expected, blue = less
stats.heatHint: Rows and columns are the numbers 1…n. Gold = together more often than expected, blue = less.
stats.pairsSummary: A pair is expected to come out together {expected} times. Pairs never drawn together: {never}. Neighbours (x, x+1): {nObs} times, expected {nExp}.
stats.pairsHint: With over a thousand pairs, some will be far above or below the expectation by chance alone — the test above says whether the whole picture is unusual.
stats.patterns: Shapes of the draws vs. all combinations
stats.patternsHint: Gold = real draws, grey = what the exact share of all combinations predicts. These are the shapes the filters cut: a filter is only useful where gold and grey differ.
stats.repeats: Numbers repeated from the previous draw
stats.repeatsHint: Expected values follow the hypergeometric distribution: the draw has no memory of the previous one.
stats.noSameDraws: No draw has ever repeated exactly.
stats.sameDrawsHint: With {combos} combinations and {draws} draws, the chance that any two draws so far are identical is {chance}. A repeat is not impossible — just rare, and excluding past results removes only a tiny share of combinations.
metric.maxEnding: Most numbers with the same last digit
metric.maxRow: Most numbers in one coupon row
metric.maxCol: Most numbers in one coupon column
filters.title: Exclusion filters
filters.intro: Every filter removes a group of combinations, and the share is exact: every combination is checked one by one. The result is computed when the tab opens and after every change.
filters.historyN: shares {n} or more numbers with a past draw
filters.honest: Filters do not raise the chance of a single ticket: over the whole history they reject exactly the same share of real results as of all combinations (filters removing 25 % of combinations would also have rejected about 25 % of past results). The gain is fewer tickets to cover and a win shared less often, because the shapes many people play are gone.
filter.odd.hint: allowed number of odd numbers (all-odd / all-even excluded by default)
filter.low.hint: allowed number from the lower half of the pool
filter.sum.hint: allowed sum of the numbers (mean ± 2 SD: only the extreme sums are out)
filter.maxDecade.hint: most numbers allowed from one decade (10–19…)
filter.maxEnding.hint: most numbers allowed with the same last digit (3, 13, 23…)
filter.maxRow.hint: most numbers allowed in one row of the coupon (popular patterns)
filter.maxCol.hint: most numbers allowed in one column of the coupon
filter.minSpread.hint: smallest allowed difference between the highest and lowest number
filter.birthdays.hint: excludes tickets made only of possible birthdays — the most shared ones
filter.history.hint: excludes past draws (and, optionally, tickets one number away from one)
filter.lastOverlap.hint: most numbers allowed from the latest draw
filter.numberWeight.hint: excludes tickets whose numbers came out rarely (average z-score below the value)
filter.pairWeight.hint: excludes tickets made of pairs that "dislike" each other (average pair z-score below the value)
generator.title: Tickets for the next draw
generator.filtersNote: Only tickets that pass the active filters (Filters tab) are generated. Of every 12 such tickets the least popular one is kept: the same chance to win, but shared with others less often.
generator.honest: Every ticket has the same chance of the jackpot as any other. With these tickets: 1 in {odds} per draw.
sim.title: Simulation — the past as an experiment
sim.intro: The app goes back in time: for every tested draw it knows only the draws before it, plays exactly as it would today (Generator tickets that pass the active filters), and only then looks at the real result. This is how to check honestly whether the filters would have helped.
sim.backtestHint: Next to the player with filters, a plain random player with the same number of tickets plays the same draws.
sim.backtestSummary: {draws} draws ({from} – {to}), {tickets} tickets each = {total} tickets per player.
sim.fixedPrizes: Fixed prizes won: strategy {a}, random {b}; each player spent {spent}.
sim.survived: The winning numbers passed the filters in {n} of {total} draws ({share}).
sim.zDiff: Difference in prizes: {diff} (z = {z}). |z| below 2 = within chance.
sim.untilHitHint: For each of the latest draws the app knows only the earlier ones. It draws the numbers one by one; a ticket that breaks the filters or was already played is not played. Every played ticket is remembered, so none repeats, until one matches the real result.
sim.unfiltered: without filters — the filters would have removed this result ({filters})
sim.avgAttempts: Average {avg} tickets to hit (from {n} draws); a jackpot is 1 in {combos}.
sim.untilHitExplain: "Expected" is the average number of tries without repeats: half of the tickets that pass the filters (systems: as many systems as needed at the bets played per system). A system plays only its bets that pass the filters and were not played yet. Knowing the past does not shorten the search for the next result — and when a filter removes the winning numbers, that result is played without filters.
about.independence.text: A certified draw machine has no memory: every combination has the same probability in every draw, whatever happened before. Hot, cold and overdue numbers describe the past, not the future. The Statistics tab tests this on the real history with chi-square tests.
about.filters.text: A filter does not change the probability of the combinations it keeps. If it removes 30 % of the combinations, it also removes on average 30 % of future winning combinations — the app measures this as "efficiency" (kept draws ÷ kept combinations), which stays near 1 for a fair draw. Filtering is still useful: it decides which part of the huge combination space your limited number of tickets covers, and it can steer you away from shapes many people play.
about.sharing.text: Pari-mutuel prizes are split between all winners. Studies of real tickets (Henze 1997; Henze and Riedwyl 1998; Crack and Whigham, NZ Lotto) show that thousands of people play 1-2-3-4-5-6, birthdays (numbers up to 31), straight lines and patterns on the coupon, and arithmetic progressions. Such tickets win as often as any other, but the prize would be shared many ways. Avoiding them raises the expected payout, not the chance of winning.
about.simulation.text: The backtest replays history as if the future were unknown (walk-forward): only earlier draws are visible, and the strategy is compared with a random player on the same draws. "Until it hits" shows how many tickets a hit takes — around the number of combinations left after filtering — and what it would cost.
about.gambler.text: After a long absence a number is not "due", and after a lucky streak it is not "used up". Martingales, systems and wheels change how money is spread, never the house edge: on average a lottery returns about half of the stake.
about.responsible.text: This app is a tool for statistics and education. It does not predict draws. Play only with money you can afford to lose; if gambling stops being fun, help is available (in Poland: 801 889 880, Anonimowi Hazardziści).

settings.dataHint: Everything — draw history, filters, settings and caches — is stored in the "data" folder inside the app's install folder, never elsewhere. Uninstalling removes it all. Nothing is sent anywhere; the only network access is downloading the draw history and checking for app updates.

mine.popularity: (1 = an average ticket; less = a win shared less often)
mine.closest: Most numbers in common with a past result: {n}. The latest such draws:
mine.alreadyDrawn: Exactly this set has been drawn before:
mine.verdict.good: A good ticket: it passes the filters and few people play it.

It only says whether the ticket passes your filters and how often a win would be shared. If your hunch says otherwise, you can still save the coupon.
bias.title: Physics of the machine and balls
bias.intro: The only way a number can really be more likely is a physical defect: a lighter, smaller or worn ball, or a machine that mixes badly. That would show as a lasting excess of a number, a change after a new ball set, or memory between draws. Each is tested here.
bias.drift: Change of a number over time (new balls / machine)
bias.bestTicket: Best ticket from the most likely balls: ×{edge} the chance of a random ticket.
bias.hint: The estimate is empirical Bayes (James–Stein): the spread of the frequencies is split into sampling noise, known exactly, and real differences between balls. With pure noise every ball is estimated at exactly the fair chance and the best ticket is ×1.000 — so a lucky-looking number is never mistaken for a heavy ball.
physics.title: What ball tolerances can do at most
physics.intro: Balls of one set are not identical: regulations allow a mass spread (Lotto NZ: 11–13 g, at most 0.45 g between the heaviest and the lightest ball; Texas: ±0.095 g of the set average). In an air-mix machine a lighter ball has a lower terminal velocity and is lifted a little more easily. This calculator turns a tolerance into the largest possible edge and the number of draws needed to even notice it.
physics.sensitivity: Effect of mass on the chance
physics.ticketSub: the {k} lightest balls vs. any ticket
physics.summary: Even at the edge of the tolerance the lightest ball would be only {edge} more likely, and it would take about {draws} draws (≈ {years} years) to see it in the results — while ball sets are checked, rotated and replaced long before that.
physics.hint: Terminal velocity v = √(2mg / ρ·Cd·A) with air density 1.2 kg/m³ and Cd = 0.47 (sphere). Detection: two-sided test at 1 % significance with 90 % power for one ball.
ev.title: Expected value of a ticket
ev.prizes: Average prizes of the other tiers (editable)
ev.summary: A ticket costs {price} and returns {back} on average: you lose {lose} per ticket in the long run.
ev.breakEven: An average ticket would pay back its price only with a jackpot of about {jackpot} (at {sold} tickets sold) — and big jackpots attract more players, which means more sharing.
ev.positive: At this jackpot a ticket returns more than its price on average (rare, and only before sharing with the extra players a jackpot like this attracts).
ev.hint: Jackpot share = (1 − e^−λ) / λ, λ = expected number of other winners of the same ticket (Poisson). 10 % tax on prizes above 2 280 zł. The average prizes of pool tiers are typical values — change them to the latest ones.
wheel.title: Abbreviated wheel (system)
wheel.intro: Pick more numbers than {k}; the app finds the fewest tickets that still guarantee a win of the chosen size whenever enough drawn numbers are among yours.
wheel.guaranteeN: {t} if {t} drawn numbers are among mine
wheel.summary: {n} tickets instead of {full} for the full system of {m} numbers: when {t} drawn numbers are among them, at least one ticket has {t} hits. Cost {cost}.
wheel.hint: The wheel is a greedy covering design. It does not change the chance of the jackpot per ticket; it spreads the tickets so that small wins are guaranteed.
wheel.hintEuro: The wheel covers the 5 main numbers; add the Euro numbers to each ticket yourself. It does not change the chance of the jackpot per ticket; it spreads the tickets so that small wins are guaranteed.

nb.title: Which number comes next to which
nb.intro: In every sorted result each number has a next higher one (in 3-12-17-28-33-41: 3→12, 12→17…). Here is how often each pair stood next to each other, against the exact chance for a fair draw.
nb.often: Next to each other most often
nb.rarely: Next to each other least often
nb.gaps: Distance to the next drawn number
nb.hint: Only pairs expected at least 5 times are ranked. Short distances are naturally the most common — the grey bars show by exactly how much.
system.title: System bet (Lotto)
system.intro: Mark {min} to {max} numbers on one bet: you play every 6-number combination of them at the normal price per combination.
system.summary: {bets} bets for {cost}; {pass} of them pass your filters. Jackpot chance per draw 1 : {odds}, any prize {any}.
system.hint: A system bet is the same as buying all its combinations separately — the same price and the same chance per combination. "Choose numbers for me" picks numbers whose combinations pass your filters as often as possible. Pool prizes (6, 5, 4) depend on the draw: "…".
settings.advanced: Advanced mode (physics, patterns, backtests, expected value, wheels)
settings.advancedHint: The simple view shows what most players need: rules, history, the generator, filters, the main statistics and the "until it hits" test. Advanced mode adds the scientific tools.
